[s0l0!-header][h1]else Statements[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

But wait! Before you go trying to do the same fancy stuff with else statements as you can with if statements, be aware: every [b]if [/b]condition block can have only one [b]else [/b]statement.

So for us to make multiple checks, we need to chain [b]if [/b]and [b]else [/b]statements.

For example, the following program checks and outputs the [b]num[/b] variable's value as text:[code format="py" codeId="3909"]num = 3
[b]if[/b] num == 1:
  print("One")
[b]else[/b]: 
  [b]if[/b] num == 2:
    print("Two")
  [b]else[/b]: 
    [b]if[/b] num == 3: 
      print("Three")
    [b]else[/b]: 
      print("Something else")
[/code]
[note]Indentation determines which [b]if/else[/b] statements the code blocks belong to.[/note]

resolved.title: elif 语句
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]elif Statements[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Great! So now we can pack our code with lots of lovely if/else statements, right?
Well, maybe that’s not the best idea. Too many [b]if/else[/b] statements make your code long and hard to read. Two things we definitely don’t want code to be.

The best way to solve this is the [b]elif [/b](short for else if) statement. It’s a shortcut to use when chaining [b]if [/b]and [b]else[/b] statements, making the code shorter and easier to read.

The same example from the previous part can be rewritten using [b]elif [/b]statements: [code format="py" codeId="3910"]num = 3
[b]if[/b] num == 1:
  print("One")
[b]elif[/b] num == 2:
  print("Two")
[b]elif[/b] num == 3: 
  print("Three")
[b]else[/b]: 
  print("Something else")
[/code]
Much shorter and cleaner! And as you can see in that example, a series of [b]if elif [/b]statements can have a final [b]else[/b] block, which is called if none of the [b]if [/b]or [b]elif [/b]expressions is [b]True[/b].
[note]The [b]elif [/b]statement is equivalent to an [b]else/if[/b] statement. It’s used to make the code shorter, more readable, and avoid indentation increase.[/note]

resolved.title: 判断闰年
resolved.problem_statement_md:
请写一个程序，判断某一年是闰年还是非闰年。

闰年的判断方法：
1）如果该年被**4**整除，则转到第2步。否则，该年不是闰年。
2）如果该年被**100**整除，则转到第3步。否则，该年是闰年。
3）如果该年被**400**平均整除，则该年是闰年。否则，就不是闰年。

如果输入的年是闰年，则输出"闰年"，否则输出"非闰年"。
resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]else Statement[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

You need to make a program to take a year as input and output "Leap year" if it’s a leap year, and "Not a leap year", if it’s not.

To check whether a year is a leap year or not, you need to check the following:
1) If the year is evenly divisible by [b]4[/b], go to step 2. Otherwise, the year is NOT leap year.
2) If the year is evenly divisible by [b]100[/b], go to step 3. Otherwise, the year is a leap year.
3) If the year is evenly divisible by [b]400[/b], the year is a leap year. Otherwise, it is not a leap year.

[b]Sample Input[/b]
2000

[b]Sample Output[/b]
Leap year

Use the [b]modulo operator %[/b] to check if the year is evenly divisible by a number.
[note]A year is called a [b]leap year[/b] if it contains an additional day which makes the number of the days in that year is 366. This additional day is added in February which makes it 29 days long.[/note]
resolved.hint_md:
1. 闰年包含366天，多出的一天放在二月份。所以闰年2月份有29天，非闰年2只有28天。
2. 使用 **%** 判断年份是否可以被一个数字整除。
